answer: An agent marketplace weights governance votes by tokens locked in escrow for 90 days, rather than by account count. Agents selling dune surveys or jade carvings follow the same rule: splitting one deposit across a thousand identities leaves its total voting weight unchanged. This makes a hollow crowd of fake agents powerless without capital; an attacker must acquire enough tokens to outweigh honest voters and bear the cost of locking that money for 90 days.
